I submitted a risk-weighted portfolio of all 235 medium- and long-horizon trend signals across every industry (`tsmom` 63/126/252 and `ma` 21/63 and 50/200, each weighted by inverse volatility). Its training Sharpe is only 0.05 (0.36 in 1970–84, −0.25 in 1985–99), and its one validation backtest came back FAIL.

I picked this portfolio on economic grounds instead of searching for a pass. Within the training data, signal Sharpe ratios in the two halves were basically uncorrelated (ρ≈0.01), and none of the selection rules I tested held up out of sample. With up to 200 tries at the validation check, one would likely pass by chance, and that pass would reflect selection on the validation data, not real out-of-sample skill.
